_what_this_is: One real recorded scan, kept because of what it refused to do. The agent under test is one of LEEVAR's own; there is no customer in this file. These are the eighteen verdicts exactly as the battery produced them, with the given names of third parties who appear in the agent's work samples replaced by [third party], and two internal tool names generalised. Nothing else was changed, and no score was touched.
_the_point: 12 of 18 probes found evidence. 12/18 = 0.6667, which is under GRADED_MIN_RATIO by three thousandths, so no letter grade is issued — the reference average over the twelve that WERE evidenced is higher than scans this battery has graded A, and the gate refused it anyway. That refusal is the thing this repository is for.
_the_defect_it_also_records: The row this came from was stored with grade "A" and composite 96.6 in the same object that says graded=false. The rendered report said PARTIAL; the machine-readable half said A. Anything gating on the number never saw the refusal. `stored_row` below is that contradiction, kept verbatim. `GradedResult` in this package is the fix: composite and grade go null, grade_withheld names the reason, and the arithmetic survives under composite_reference where no caller can mistake it for a result.

_why_the_reference_number_moved: The stored row's reference composite is 96.6; this package computes 96.2 from the identical verdicts. Neither is a typo. 96.6 is the mean over the six DIMENSIONS, and D3 and D5 each rest on a single surviving probe, so each of those single probes carried a full sixth of the score. The composite here is weighted by evidenced PROBES, which removes the reward for measuring less: a dimension resting on one probe contributes one probe's worth. Measured across four internal self-scans, the old arithmetic paid for thinness monotonically — dimensions with 3 probes left averaged 88.4, with 2 left 90.4, with 1 left 97.9. See the long comment in grade-battery.ts.
